providers.notes: Largest IOU in Hawaii; serves ~95% of Oahu population. Energy efficiency rebates administered through third-party program Hawaii Energy (Leidos). Parent company Hawaiian Electric Industries (HEI).
HEI subsidiary serving Hawaii Island. Commercial efficiency rebates delivered via Hawaii Energy (Leidos). Shares tariff structure parallel to HECO with island-specific schedules.
HEI subsidiary; serves roughly 72,000 customers across Maui, Lanai, and Molokai. Commercial efficiency rebates delivered via Hawaii Energy (Leidos).

Consumer-owned cooperative; the only Hawaiian island not served by HEI. Kauai customers are NOT eligible for Hawaii Energy rebates. KIUC runs its own commercial energy efficiency and EV charging programs.

programs.stacking_rules: Cannot stack prescriptive and custom rebates for the same measure
programs.funding_status: Open — available through June 30, 2026, while funding lasts (first-come, first-served)
programs.program_notes_ai: Program year runs July 1, 2025–June 30, 2026. Covers HVAC, lighting (LED), refrigeration, kitchen equipment, water heating, motors/VFDs, compressed air, cool roofs, and more. LED lighting rebates for most fixtures end March 1, 2026 due to Hawaii's fluorescent lighting ban (Act 225). DLC listing required for LED products. Administered by Leidos on behalf of Hawaiian Electric, HELCO, and MECO. Available to ratepayers on Oahu, Hawaii Island, Maui, Molokai, and Lanai only.

programs.stacking_rules: Cannot stack prescriptive and custom rebates for the same measure
programs.funding_status: Open — available through June 30, 2026, while funding lasts (first-come, first-served)
programs.program_notes_ai: Same program as HECO — Hawaii Energy (Leidos) administers across all HEI islands. Hawaii Island ratepayers eligible. Same measure categories and DLC requirements apply.

programs.stacking_rules: Cannot stack prescriptive and custom rebates for the same measure
programs.funding_status: Open — available through June 30, 2026, while funding lasts (first-come, first-served)
programs.program_notes_ai: Same statewide Hawaii Energy program covering Maui, Molokai, and Lanai ratepayers. Same measure categories, DLC requirements, and program year (July 2025–June 2026).

programs.program_name: Hawaii Energy Commercial Custom / Customized Projects (2025)
programs.stacking_rules: Custom and prescriptive rebates cannot be combined for the same measure
programs.funding_status: Open — available through June 30, 2026, while funding lasts
programs.program_notes_ai: Custom rebates are based on projected first-year energy savings and peak demand reduction. Incentives can be up to 50% of project costs. Pre-approval required before any work begins — projects started without approval are at significant risk of disqualification. Case-by-case evaluation; may require pre- and post-installation metering, engineering calculations, and on-site inspection. Contact energy advisor at HawaiiEnergy@leidos.com.

programs.program_name: Hawaii Energy Power Move Commercial Energy Storage (2025)
required_documents: Completed Hawaii Energy Commercial Incentive Application (signed by HECO account holder)
System Operating / Reporting Data (minimum 7 days of discharge data)
programs.stacking_rules: Can be combined with HECO Battery Bonus program enrollment (encouraged but not required). If opted into another HECO program, Hawaii Energy defers to HECO's established rules.
programs.funding_status: Open — check program rules for current cycle
programs.program_notes_ai: Incentivizes commercial energy storage installations on Oahu and Maui to reduce load during the evening peak (5–9 p.m.). Customers must operate and/or export stored electricity during committed time period for a minimum of 2 years from installation. HECO Battery Bonus enrollment is strongly encouraged. EV charging station rebates also available for qualifying installations between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2027; contact hawaiienergyEVCS@leidos.com.

programs.program_name: HECO EnergyScout Small Business Direct Load Control (2025)
programs.funding_status: Closed — not currently accepting new participants; interest list available
programs.program_notes_ai: Small Business Direct Load Control (SBDLC) provides $5/month per enrolled water heater and $5/ton of enrolled A/C capacity. HECO installs control device at no cost. Program is not accepting new participants as of 2025/2026; customers may join interest list by emailing energyscout@hawaiianelectric.com.

programs.program_name: HECO EnergyScout Commercial & Industrial Direct Load Control (2025)
programs.funding_status: Closed — not currently accepting new participants; see Fast Demand Response program
programs.program_notes_ai: Large C&I customers typically commit 50 kW–5 MW of curtailable load and receive monthly bill credits regardless of whether a demand response event occurs. HECO transfers load to customer's on-site emergency generators. Not accepting new participants; large customers directed to Fast Demand Response program.

programs.program_name: HECO Backup Power Rebate Program — Commercial (2025, Proposed)
programs.funding_status: Pending PUC Approval — proposed two-year pilot submitted to Hawaii PUC October 2025
programs.program_notes_ai: Proposed two-year pilot to offer $400/kW rebate for commercial purchases of generators or batteries. $3M annual budget across all five HEI-served islands. Priority given to commercial customers in PSPS (Public Safety Power Shutoff) zones. Maui County ~50%, Hawaii Island ~40%, Oahu ~10% of funding. Commercial customers may receive up to $120,000 example rebate for a 300 kW generator capacity upgrade. Businesses that receive rebates may be called upon to act as 'resilience hubs' to offset grid load. As of 2025, pending PUC approval — not yet active.

programs.program_name: KIUC Commercial Energy Efficiency Retrofit Program (2025)
programs.rebate_payment_method: Direct Incentive (not a rebate — program explicitly states it does not offer rebates)
programs.program_notes_ai: Incentives range from 50–100% of project costs to promote energy-saving measures including A/C, motors, refrigeration, and lighting controls. A total resource cost test is performed to determine feasibility. Customer must work with a KIUC-approved Trade Ally or Supplier. All projects must be submitted for pre-approval to verify eligibility and available funds before KIUC approves the incentive agreement.

programs.program_name: KIUC Commercial New Construction Energy Efficiency Program (2025)
programs.program_notes_ai: Applies only to new construction after plans are completed. Any changes to plans per discussions with KIUC to purchase more energy-efficient equipment qualify. Customer must work with KIUC-approved Trade Ally.

programs.program_name: KIUC Commercial EV Charging Station Rebate Program (2025)
programs.stacking_rules: Can be combined with Hawaii Energy EV charging rebates ($4,500 New Level / $3,000 Retrofit Level) for a potential combined total
programs.program_notes_ai: Commercial incentive: $10,000 rebate for a new Level II Multi-Port EV Charger when materials and installation costs exceed $45,000. Chargers subject to visual verification / field audit. KIUC reserves right to change rebate levels without notice. Submit to KIUC Energy Services, 4463 Pahee St., Suite 1, Lihue, HI 96766 or energyservices@kiuc.coop.

rate_schedules.description: Standard general service schedule for Oahu commercial and industrial customers. Includes energy charge, demand charge, and customer charge components plus ECAC and other riders.
rate_schedules.notes: Primary commercial tariff for Oahu (HECO). Specific $/kWh and $/kW values are set by PUC order and updated periodically via transmittal letters; consult the effective rate summary at hawaiianelectric.com for current figures.

rate_schedules.description: Time-of-use version of Schedule J for Oahu commercial customers. Energy charges vary by on-peak and off-peak periods. Includes demand charge computed on billing demand.
rate_schedules.notes: Governed by Docket No. 2019-0323, Order 41220 filed November 22, 2024. Demand charge calculated on kW of billing demand per minimum charge specification.

rate_schedules.description: Large power service for high-demand Oahu commercial and industrial customers. Separate metering may be elected for EV charging under Schedule EV-P.
rate_schedules.notes: Commercial facilities may maintain Schedule P or elect Schedule EV-P for separately metered EV charging under the five-year TOU pilot (2022–2027).

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule ARD TOU-J — Advanced Rate Design TOU
rate_schedules.description: Advanced Rate Design time-of-use schedule for Oahu commercial customers under Docket 2019-0323. Non-fuel energy charge component of 14.4626 cents/kWh noted in tariff sheets.
rate_schedules.notes: Governed by Docket No. 2019-0323; transmittal letter dated October 15, 2025. The 14.4626 cents/kWh is a non-fuel energy charge component only — total rate includes ECAC and other surcharges.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule EV-J — Commercial EV Charging TOU
rate_schedules.description: Five-year TOU pilot rate (2022–2027) for separately metered commercial EV charging on Oahu. Incentivizes mid-day charging when solar generation is high. Requires separate dedicated meter.
rate_schedules.notes: Available to businesses, workplaces, and multi-unit dwellings. Governed by Docket No. 2022-0212; transmittal letter October 24, 2025. Includes Energy Charge, Customer Charge, and Demand Charge components.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule E-Bus-P — Electric Bus Large Power TOU
rate_schedules.description: Special TOU rate for electric bus charging under Schedule P service. All surcharges applicable to Schedule P also apply. Governed by Decision and Order No. 41959 dated September 26, 2025.
rate_schedules.notes: Transmittal letter dated March 18, 2026. Non-fuel energy charge on a TOU basis. Intended for large commercial transit/fleet operators.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule EV-P — Commercial EV Charging Large Power TOU
rate_schedules.description: TOU pilot rate for large commercial EV charging facilities (Level 2 and DCFC) served under Schedule P. Requires separate dedicated meter. Mitigates high demand charges.
rate_schedules.notes: Five-year pilot program (2022–2027). Available on Oahu, Maui County, and Hawaii Island. Commercial facilities may maintain Schedule P or switch to EV-P for EV charging meter.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule G — General Light and Power Service
rate_schedules.description: Primary commercial and industrial general service tariff for Kauai. Not applicable to master-metered multi-family residential or shared commercial meters except in conservation-promoting circumstances. Includes Energy Rate Adjustment Clause (ERAC) for fuel and purchased energy cost recovery.
rate_schedules.notes: Fourth Revised Sheet 70, effective May 9, 2025. Governed by KIUC Tariff No. 1, Decision and Order No. 41688. Specific $/kWh and customer charge values are included in the tariff PDF.

rate_schedules.description: KIUC rates index page listing all approved tariff schedules for Kauai residential, commercial, and industrial customers including Schedule G and other commercial schedules.
rate_schedules.notes: KIUC strives to deliver electricity at the lowest possible cost. Rates based on cost of generating/delivering power, infrastructure maintenance, and community programs.

forms.form_notes: Effective July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Must be submitted within 6 months of invoice/sales receipt. Application should be filled out completely and, when possible, submitted before equipment installation. Covers both prescriptive and custom project tracks.
Same statewide Hawaii Energy application form. Effective July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Must be submitted within 6 months of invoice.
Same statewide Hawaii Energy application form used for MECO-territory commercial customers. Effective July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.

forms.program_name: Hawaii Energy Commercial Custom / Customized Projects (2025)
forms.form_notes: Same application PDF used for custom projects. Must be accompanied by pre-approval request, project specifications, engineering calculations, and pre/post metering data. Submit to HawaiiEnergy@leidos.com or assigned Energy Advisor.

forms.program_name: Hawaii Energy Power Move Commercial Energy Storage (2025)
forms.form_name: Hawaii Energy Commercial Incentive Application (Energy Storage)
forms.form_notes: Must be signed by the HECO account holder. Must be accompanied by minimum 7 days of system discharge operating data proving compliance with energy capacity and scheduling commitments.
Required for all Hawaii Energy commercial incentive applications. Hawaii Energy reports all applicable incentive payments to the IRS on Form 1099.

Last updated July 1, 2026. Four-page commercial rebate summary listing all prescriptive measures, incentive levels, and eligibility notes for program year 2026. Used as reference alongside the main application.

forms.program_name: KIUC Commercial EV Charging Station Rebate Program (2025)
forms.form_notes: Submit completed application with approved County permits, proof of purchase, and proof of installation to KIUC Energy Services (4463 Pahee St., Suite 1, Lihue, HI 96766) or email energyservices@kiuc.coop. Chargers subject to visual verification/field audit.
